source_refs.note: Book p. 31-32: 2.5 Real Life Applications, Growth and Decay in Finance (Predicting Long-Term Stock Prices), Examples 12-13

blocks.text: Ab tak humne graphs banaye aur un ke milne ke points dhoonde. Is aakhri hisse mein dekhenge ke functions asal zindagi mein kahan kaam aate hain: paisa kaise barhta hai, aur aaloodgi (pollution) waqt ke saath kaise kam hoti hai. Kitab "2.5" ke foran baad yeh heading deti hai:
Growth and Decay in Finance (Predicting Long-Term Stock Prices)

Jab koi cheez waqt ke saath miqdaar ya size mein barhti hai to use growth (barhotri) kehte hain. Misal ke taur par bank account mein rakha paisa jis par interest (munafa) milta hai aur woh barhta jata hai, ya khargoshon ki aabadi jo maheenon mein barhti jati hai.

Jab koi cheez waqt ke saath miqdaar ya size mein kam hoti hai to use decay (ghatao) kehte hain. Misal ke taur par radioactive maadda saalon mein apni taqat khota hai, ya garam coffee ka cup waqt ke saath thanda hota jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Exponential growth ka formula \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\) hai, jahan \(r > 0\). Is ke har hisse ko samjhiye:
\(P_{0}\) shuru ki qeemat hai (kyun ke \(t = 0\) par \(e^{0} = 1\), to \(P(0) = P_{0}\));
\(r\) rate hai, decimal mein (5% = 0.05);
\(e \approx 2.71828\) ek khaas number hai, jaise \(\pi\).
Is growth ki khaasiyat yeh hai ke qeemat tez se tez barhti hai, kyun ke har saal ka izafa ek bari raqam ka percentage hota hai (sood par sood).
Jab \(t\) power (exponent) mein ho aur use nikaalna ho to natural logarithm \(\ln\) lete hain, jo \(e\) ka ulat hai: agar \(e^{k} = a\) to \(k = \ln a\).
Decay is ka ulta hai: miqdaar waqt ke saath ghat'ti hai, jaise Example 13 mein.

blocks.title: Example 12
blocks.problem:
The value of a stock follows the exponential growth model \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\), where \(P_{0}\) is the initial stock price, \(r\) is the growth rate per year and \(t\) is the time in years. Suppose a stock is currently valued at Rs. 5,000, and it is expected to grow at a rate of 5% per year.
(i) Find the value of the stock after 10 years.
(ii) After how many years will the stock double in value?
steps:
Given: \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\), jahan \(P_{0} = 5{,}000\) aur \(r = 0.05\) (5% growth rate).
To find: (i) \(P(10)\); (ii) woh waqt \(t\) jab \(P(t) = 2P_{0}\) ho jaye.
Method: sab se pehle dekhte hain ke yahan do alag sawal hain. (i) mein bas values formula mein rakhni hain. (ii) mein \(t\) power (exponent) mein chhupa hua hai, us ko neeche laane ke liye natural logarithm (\(\ln\)) lena parega.

Step 1: (i) \(t = 10\) rakhein
Exponential growth ka formula \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\) hai. Yahan \(P_{0} = 5{,}000\), \(r = 0.05\) aur \(t = 10\) saal.
\[P(10) = 5{,}000\, e^{0.05 \times 10}\]
\[= 5{,}000\, e^{0.5}\]
Kyun: 5% ka matlab hai \(\frac{5}{100} = 0.05\); formula mein rate hamesha decimal mein jata hai. Aur \(0.05 \times 10 = 0.5\). (Kitab yahan 5,000 ko ghalti se "5.000" chhaap deti hai; neeche "Kitab ki ghalti" dekhiye.)

Step 2: (i) Value nikaalein
\(e^{0.5} \approx 1.6487\) istemal karte hue:
\[P(10) = 5{,}000 \times 1.6487\]
\[\approx 8244\]
Kyun: \(e \approx 2.71828\) ek khaas number hai jo qudrati (natural) growth mein aata hai. Calculator par \(e^{x}\) wala button dabayein: \(e^{0.5} \approx 1.6487\). Poori value \(8243.6\) aati hai jo round kar ke Rs. 8244 banti hai. Yani 10 saal mein paise taqreeban 65% barh gaye.

Step 3: (ii) Dugna hone ki shart likhein
Humein woh \(t\) chahiye jab stock dugna ho jaye, yani \(P(t) = 2P_{0}\). Equation:
\[2P_{0} = P_{0}e^{rt}\]
Dono sides ko \(P_{0}\) se divide karne par
\[2 = e^{rt}\]
Kyun: "double in value" ka matlab hai shuru wali qeemat ka dugna. \(P_{0}\) dono taraf hai, is liye cancel ho gaya. Is ka dilchasp matlab: dugna hone ka waqt shuru ki raqam par munhasir nahin; 5,000 ho ya 5 lakh, waqt wahi lagega.

Step 4: (ii) Natural logarithm lein
\[\ln 2 = rt\]
Kyun: \(\ln\) aur \(e\) ek doosre ka ulat (inverse) hain, jaise square aur square root. \(\ln(e^{rt}) = rt\). Is tarah \(t\) power se neeche aa jata hai aur ab aam equation ki tarah hal ho sakta hai.

Step 5: (ii) \(t\) nikaalein
\[t = \dfrac{\ln 2}{r} = \dfrac{0.6931}{0.05}\]
\[t \approx 13.86\]
Kyun: \(\ln 2 \approx 0.6931\) (calculator). \(0.05\) se divide karna 20 se multiply karne ke barabar hai: \(0.6931 \times 20 = 13.862\). (Kitab yahan division ka nishaan chhaapna bhool gayi hai aur "0.69310.05" likha hai; sahi \(0.6931 / 0.05\) hai.)

Tasdeeq:
(i) \(\ln(8244 / 5000) = \ln 1.6488 \approx 0.5\), jo \(0.05 \times 10\) hi hai.
(ii) \(e^{0.05 \times 13.86} = e^{0.693} \approx 2.00\). Yani 13.86 saal baad qeemat waqai dugni hai. Dono jawab durust hain.
blocks.answer:
(i) 10 saal baad stock ki qeemat taqreeban Rs. 8244 hogi.
(ii) Stock taqreeban 13.86 saal mein dugna ho jayega.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text:
Example 12 ke hal mein do chhapai ki ghaltiyan hain:
(i) kitab \(P(10) = 5.000\, e^{0.05 \times 10}\) chhaapti hai, yani 5,000 ki jagah decimal wala "5.000". Sahi \(5{,}000\, e^{0.05 \times 10}\) (paanch hazaar) hai, jaisa agle hi qadam mein likha hai.
(ii) kitab \(t = \ln 2 / r = 0.69310.05 = 13.86\) chhaapti hai, jis mein division ka nishaan gaayab hai. Sahi \(t = \ln 2 / r = 0.6931 / 0.05 = 13.86\) hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari practice hai (kitab ka sawal nahin): agar Rs. 10,000 saalana 7% ki exponential growth se barhein to kitne saal mein dugne honge?
\(t = \frac{\ln 2}{r} = \frac{0.6931}{0.07} \approx 9.9\) saal.
Ek aasan andaza (rule of 70): dugna hone ka waqt \(\approx 70 \div\) (percentage rate). Yahan \(70 \div 7 = 10\) saal, aur Example 12 mein \(70 \div 5 = 14\) saal, jo 13.86 ke bohat qareeb hai. Yeh rule sirf andaze ke liye hai; exam mein poora formula likhein.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Agla sawal decay ka hai. Ghor karein ke Example 13 ka function \(e\) wala nahin, balke \(\frac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\) hai: har decay exponential nahin hota. Is function ko samajhne ke liye do baatein dekhiye. Pehli: \(t = 0\) par \(C(0) = \frac{100}{\sqrt{1}} = 100\) ppm, yani shuru ki aaloodgi 100 ppm thi. Doosri: \(t\) jitna barhta hai, denominator \(\sqrt{t + 1}\) utna bara hota hai, aur bare number se divide karne par jawab chhota aata hai. Is liye concentration hamesha ghat'ti rehti hai, magar zero kabhi nahin hoti; bas zero ke qareeb aati jati hai.

blocks.title: Example 13
blocks.problem:
The concentration of a pollutant in a lake, in parts per million (ppm), decays over time according to the function
\[C(t) = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\]
where \(t\) is the time in days since the pollutant was introduced.
(i) What is the concentration of the pollutant after 4 days?
(ii) After how many days will the concentration drop below 10 ppm?
steps:
Given: \(C(t) = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\), \(t\) dinon mein.
To find: (i) \(C(4)\); (ii) kitne din baad \(C(t) < 10\) ho jayega.
Method: (i) mein seedha \(t = 4\) rakhna hai. (ii) mein pehle woh din dhoondenge jab \(C(t)\) theek 10 ho (kitab bhi \(C(t) = 10\) rakhti hai), phir dekhenge ke waqt ke saath \(C\) kam hota hai ya zyada.

Step 1: (i) 4 din baad concentration
Pollutant ki concentration ka function \(C(t) = \frac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\) hai, jahan \(t\) dinon mein waqt hai.
\[C(4) = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{4 + 1}} = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{5}}\]
\[\approx 44.72 \text{ ppm}\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{5} \approx 2.2361\), aur \(100 / 2.2361 \approx 44.72\).
Dhyan dein: \(+1\) square root ke andar hai, is liye pehle \(4 + 1 = 5\), phir root. \(\sqrt{4} + 1 = 3\) likhna ghalat hoga.

Step 2: (ii) \(C(t) = 10\) rakhein
\[10 = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\]
\[\Rightarrow \sqrt{t + 1} = 10\]
Kyun: dono sides ko \(\sqrt{t + 1}\) se multiply kiya aur phir 10 se divide kiya: \(\sqrt{t + 1} = 100 / 10 = 10\). Is tarah unknown denominator se nikal kar upar aa gaya.

Step 3: (ii) Square kar ke hal karein
\[t + 1 = 100\]
\[\Rightarrow t = 99\]
Kyun: square karne se square root khatam ho jata hai. Dono sides positive hain, is liye koi faltu (extra) jawab paida nahin hota.

Step 4: (ii) Matlab samjhein
\(t = 99\) par concentration theek 10 ppm hai. Jaise jaise \(t\) barhta hai, \(\sqrt{t + 1}\) barhta hai aur fraction \(\frac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}}\) chhota hota jata hai. Is liye 99 din ke baad concentration 10 ppm se kam ho jati hai.
Kyun: sawal "below 10" yani 10 se kam ka poochta hai. Sirf barabari wala din nikaal lena kaafi nahin; yeh bhi dekhna zaroori hai ke function kis taraf ja raha hai (yahan decay hai, yani kam ho raha hai).

Tasdeeq:
\[C(99) = \dfrac{100}{\sqrt{100}} = 10\]
\[C(120) = \dfrac{100}{11} \approx 9.09 < 10\]
Aur \(C(4) = 44.72\) bhi \(C(0) = 100\) aur \(C(99) = 10\) ke darmiyan hai, jaisa ek ghatte (decreasing) function mein hona chahiye.
blocks.answer:
(i) 4 din baad concentration taqreeban 44.72 ppm hai.
(ii) 99 din ke baad concentration 10 ppm se kam ho jayegi (\(t = 99\) par yeh theek 10 ppm hai).

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Example 13 mein concentration 50 ppm kab hogi? (Jawab: \(\frac{100}{\sqrt{t + 1}} = 50 \Rightarrow \sqrt{t + 1} = 2 \Rightarrow t = 3\) din.) Ghor karein: 100 se 50 tak sirf 3 din lage, magar 50 se 10 tak 96 din. Yani shuru mein tezi se safai hoti hai aur baad mein bohat aahista.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Growth: miqdaar waqt ke saath barhti hai; decay: ghat'ti hai.
2. Exponential growth \(P(t) = P_{0}e^{rt}\): rate decimal mein likhein; \(P(0) = P_{0}\).
3. Dugna hone ka waqt: \(t = \frac{\ln 2}{r} \approx \frac{0.6931}{r}\), shuru ki raqam kuch bhi ho.
4. Power mein chhupa variable nikaalne ke liye dono sides ka \(\ln\) lein.
5. "Se kam / se zyada" wale sawal mein pehle barabari hal karein, phir dekhein function barh raha hai ya ghat raha hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(r = 0.05\) ki jagah \(r = 5\) rakh dena: percentage ko hamesha 100 se divide karein.
2. \(\ln(e^{rt})\) ko \(rt\) ki jagah kuch aur likh dena, ya aakhir mein \(r\) se divide karna bhool jana.
3. Example 13 mein \(C(4) = 100/\sqrt{4} + 1\) likh dena: \(+1\) root ke andar hai, \(\sqrt{4 + 1} = \sqrt{5}\).
4. Bohat jaldi round kar dena: \(e^{0.5}\) aur \(\ln 2\) ke chaar decimal aakhir tak rakhein, warna jawab thora hil jata hai.
